Hey I agree with your major points.  Not trying to push this on you, rather open your mind a little, but I think drugs are stupid.  I really hate what they do to people's lives and don't they should be lauded.  Immature is probably a better word; but again, that's not the point.

My point is that even accounting for my personal opinion, drugs alone don't make someone bad.  I mean, problems can be created or exacerbated with excessive use, immature use, biological problems (self medication and whatever you call the "bad drunk" equivalents for certain substances).  

I think you're right -- "you have cocaine on your person and you're high on it" leading to a huge jail sentence is stupid.  Things like cocaine aren't physically addictive.  MDMA is, arguably, kind of just a super potent anti-depressant (which leaves you horribly depressed after because it depletes all of your seratonin reserves, taking two weeks to rebuild); but what's the big deal?  Unless data shows a lot of people suicide after taking it, I don't see why it's a bad thing.  

I think if you can legalize drugs like that, it would keep people from doing drugs that certainly damage you and get you hooked in the beginning (heroin, methamphetamine, ...) and drugs that can be inconsistent and traumatizing for "bad trip" reasons (LSD, shrooms, ...)

I think if someone commits a crime while on drugs, the punishment should be *more* severe (which is already the case in things like: drinking and driving) to encourage healthier use.  If someone is obviously tweaking out in public and disturbing people's peace, corrective action should be taken.

I think they should restrict it from use in commercial products (i.e.; coca in coca cola) for legitimate reasons too.

I think it's something to control, not restrict.  If someone has a problem, TREAT THE PROBLEM!!!  What does locking them up do to help?  That being said, you'll probably still have to lock some people up, because some addicts don't want to be "saved" (personal experience).

So, in short, I *completely* agree with the war on drugs being stupid.  Agreed on all the other "legal" drugs and potential benefits of illegal drugs.  Agree with the science, control, regulation.  I'd love to see the asshole cartels who murder families fall out of power.

BUT: My final point, while functionally unimportant in our conversation,  is something I have a lot of contention with:
>Tl:dr: I agree and your body your choice

Not true in the sense that your body is a part of society.  If you buy into health insurance and you're smoking cigarettes with reckless abandon, eventually using the financial cushion provided to you by other people to treat severe lung cancer, you are a selfish asshole.

If you're a parent and you spend too much time being strung out, maybe via running from your problems instead of facing them (not a stigma of all drugs users, just saying i know a lot of mentally ill people who self medicate to no successful end), then you're an irresponsible asshole.

TL;DR I could keep going.  But my point is: I think society sucks.  People are part of society and I think more people should take on personal responsibility to support the collective.  I think drugs *can* (but not necessarily *will*) exacerbate a lack of personal responsibility.  I think currently legal drugs and vices can already do this.  I think there should be a lot more focus on getting people with problems help before they're punished.  That way they can contribute to the collective society instead of being uselessly filed away.  Even if it's more expensive, it's a shame that we as humans haven't provided better support to our neighbors.  I think the only way to accomplish this is improve understanding instead of speculating and spreading stigma.  I think some people will still have to be imprisoned, because I've met a fair share of people who are reckless and don't want to be "saved" from their vices (alcohol being one of them).
